title: Do taking away five negatives and adding five positives match?
description: Seven negative tokens are changed in two ways: five negative tokens are taken away, or five positive tokens are added. Both ways leave the same two negative tokens. Keeko thinks taking away must make a number smaller and adding must make it bigger, so they cannot match.
teaching_notes: One idea: taking away negative tokens gives the same value as adding the same number of positive tokens. Watch for students who think taking away always lowers a value.

video_script.why: The child compares taking away negative tokens with adding positive tokens and sees that both leave the same value.
video_script.substitution: Do the subtraction by taking tokens away, do the addition by cancelling zero pairs, and compare the tokens that stay.
video_script.anchor: seven negative tokens on the board
video_script.wrong_answer: taking away always makes a number smaller
video_script.wrong_move: believes taking away always lowers a value and adding always raises it, so the two cannot match
maths_rules: (−7) − (−5): take away 5 of the 7 negative tokens, 7 − 5 = 2 negative tokens stay, so −2
(−7) + (+5): 5 positive tokens cancel 5 of the 7 negative tokens as 5 zero pairs, 2 negative tokens stay, so −2
slip: taking away negative tokens raises the value, from −7 to −2
video_script.design: One idea: both ways leave the same tokens, so subtracting a negative gives the same value as adding the matching positive. Positive tokens are green and negative tokens are red as in the book. Keeko's doubt is that taking away always makes a number smaller.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the two ways cannot match, because taking away always makes a number smaller.
<bookmark mark='up'/>But look at the pile again. Taking away red tokens moved the value up, from negative seven to negative two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Red tokens are worth less than zero, so removing them makes the value go up.
